reason: Both fully satisfy the hard requirements (heading order, snapshot-before-risk, no restart/failover before snapshot, explicit abort/rollback conditions), but Response B is more technically precise and actionable — it notes using crash-consistent hot-backup mechanisms (e.g., pg_start_backup/xtrabackup) when a live snapshot isn't clean, gives a concrete replication-lag threshold before promotion, and states a clearer, more emphatic 'hard gate' callout for the no-restart/no-failover-before-snapshot rule. Response A is equally compliant but relies on more generic, less concrete guidance.
